solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Revolutionary, not vice-versa? Not revolutionary at all!

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns things over completely, so the letters of the following words are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A paradoxical musing on whether a radical is merely the reverse of a traditionalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a noun for a rebel, but it signals that NOTVICEVERSA is rearranged; the closing exclamation is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditionalist resists change, the very opposite of anything revolutionary.

clue.text: Figure from a month ago, finally overdrawn

parts.note: Oct is the short form of October

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word overdrawn

explanation.surface: A bank statement figure from a month back, showing the account at last went into the red.
explanation.definitionFit: An eight-sided polygon is a geometric figure.

clue.text: Uncomfortable, like a woolly jumper?

definitions.meaning: awkward and embarrassed, as someone caught out feels
a woolly jumper playfully describes a sheep, an animal that leaps and wears wool; resembling one

explanation.surface: Someone squirming in an itchy knitted sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper is the British word for a sweater, but here it is an animal that jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: Embarrassed awkwardness is the usual sense; the second reading is the literal 'resembling a ewe or ram'.

clue.text: Part of film seen at the ceilidh most likely

definitions.meaning: a spool holding a section of cinema film

definitions.text: seen at the ceilidh most likely
definitions.meaning: a lively Scottish dance, typical at a ceilidh

explanation.surface: A clip of footage shot at a Scottish folk evening.
explanation.walkthrough: A ceilidh is a Scottish or Irish social gathering with folk music and dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names a spool of film and a fast Scottish country dance.

clue.text: Secretary of a Premier club (with three points) is taken on

indicators.note: taken on means added at the end, so the word is goes after the rest

parts.note: Man U is Manchester United, a Premier League football club
E, N and S are three points of the compass

explanation.surface: A football club's secretary is hired just as the team picks up three league points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three points' looks like a football win but means compass points; Man U is the common name for Manchester United.
explanation.definitionFit: An amanuensis is a scribe or assistant who takes dictation, a secretary.

clue.text: Kind of sugar to be avoided by pilots

definitions.meaning: fine powdered sugar used for frosting cakes
ice forming on an aircraft's wings, a known hazard in flight

explanation.surface: A health warning that pilots should cut out sweet things.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the fine powdered sugar is named after the topping it makes.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a cake-topping sugar and ice building up on wings, a danger to aircraft.

clue.text: Moral of the CIA is rubbished on-line

indicators.note: rubbished means trashed or knocked about, so the letters of the CIA are jumbled

parts.note: read as 'on line': L stands for line and is put on, at the end

explanation.surface: The moral code of the CIA being mocked on the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubbished' makes ETHICA from THECIA; 'on-line' looks like the internet but gives L added on.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethical and moral are synonyms describing right conduct.

clue.text: It brought capital relief in the forties

definitions.text: It brought capital relief in the forties

parts.words: It brought capital relief in the forties
parts.note: the 1948-49 Allied flights supplying blockaded West Berlin, a city then cut off by Soviet forces

explanation.surface: Something that brought excellent relief during the 1940s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like 'excellent' but refers to the German capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1948-49 operation flew food and fuel into the blockaded German city, relieving it.

clue.text: After victory over Germany at sea, this is welcome

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above, so the win piece sits on top of the Germany piece

parts.note: following means coming after
a win is a victory
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: Winning against Germany at sea is welcome news, a wartime naval story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After victory over Germany' suggests VE Day, but it is all wordplay; the definition is the sailor's view.
explanation.definitionFit: A breeze blowing from behind helps a sailing ship along, so mariners welcome it.

clue.text: Hardline former army corps takes central control

indicators.note: takes means holds inside, so the former army corps wraps around the middle of control

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British army corps

indicators.note: central picks out the middle letter of the word control

explanation.surface: A hardline ex-military corps seizing power in a coup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Former army corps' is best read as one unit, ex-REME, the British Army's Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, which then 'takes' the central letter of control inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme and hardline both describe uncompromising, far-out positions.

clue.text: Involuntary expulsion from a paper reported

indicators.note: reported signals that the words a paper are swapped for a phrase spoken out loud

parts.note: a tissue is a thin sheet of soft paper

explanation.surface: Someone forced out of a newspaper's staff, as the press reports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expulsion from a paper' suggests a sacked journalist; the definition is a sneeze, and saying 'a tissue' gives its sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The written sound of a sneeze, an involuntary expulsion of air through nose and mouth.

clue.text: A helping hand, paradoxically

parts.note: a boost given to someone, oddly named after a lower limb though it means assistance from a hand

explanation.surface: Offering assistance in a contradictory way.
explanation.walkthrough: The paradox is that a 'hand' is here called by the name of a different limb.
explanation.definitionFit: A boost upward, literally lifting someone by the knee, figuratively any assistance.

clue.text: Kind of operation on French soldier's lower leg, mostly

parts.note: sur is French for on
a GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: the calf is the back of the lower leg

explanation.surface: A French soldier's lower leg being operated on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims CALF to CAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A precise, targeted strike is described as a surgical operation, as is one done by a surgeon.

clue.text: Is calendar reform needed for these people?

indicators.note: to reform is to reshape or reorganise, so the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: read with the spelling calender, a machine for pressing cloth or paper, which supplies the second E the printed calendar lacks

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a nation's calendar needs changing.
explanation.walkthrough: As printed, 'Is calendar' has one A too many and one E too few for the answer; the anagram works with the spelling 'calender', which was likely intended or mistyped.
explanation.definitionFit: The citizens of the North Atlantic island nation are the people referred to.

clue.text: Grandma takes ring back for an instant

parts.note: nan is an informal word for grandmother
O is shaped like a ring
to second a proposal is to back or support it

explanation.surface: Grandma quickly takes back her ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like a reversal signal, but it means support.
explanation.definitionFit: A billionth of a second is an extremely brief instant.

clue.text: The grey beast retreats — you may go with it!

indicators.note: retreats means goes backwards, so the beast's name is read in reverse

parts.note: the grey wolf is a wild animal of the dog family

explanation.surface: A grey animal backs off, and you might follow it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the phrase 'go with the' current, meaning to conform.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'go with the current' means to follow the crowd; here the stream itself is meant.

clue.text: Its ranks need training in an ancient language

indicators.note: ranks that need training are not yet in order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An army's ranks requiring drill in an old tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: The classical language of ancient India, used for Hindu scriptures.

clue.text: Single mother could be a religious leader

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
mam is a dialect word for mother

explanation.surface: A single mother might become a cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: A Muslim prayer leader in a mosque is a religious leader.

clue.text: Twin boys first to arrive in Lucerne

indicators.note: twin means there are two of the same, so the boy's name is given twice

parts.note: Alf is a boy's name, short for Alfred

indicators.note: first to picks out the opening letter of the word arrive

explanation.surface: Twin boys are the first to arrive in the Swiss city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lucerne' looks like the Swiss city, but it is the name for a fodder plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucerne is the British name for the clover-like fodder crop Americans call by this other name.

clue.text: Former language of a pope, usually

definitions.meaning: the earlier form of the tongue spoken in Italy
popes have mostly been elderly men from Italy

explanation.surface: The tongue a pope traditionally used.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase as an adjective plus a nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: Both readings fit: an older stage of the Romance language, and an aged man from Rome's country.

clue.text: Devastated hearing where archaeologist's interests lie

definitions.meaning: archaeologists dig among the remains of ancient buildings

explanation.surface: An archaeologist crushed by a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing' acts as a link here: the phrase is heard both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrecked things lie destroyed, and old sites of interest lie as crumbling remains.

clue.text: You must drive one home the other way

definitions.text: You must drive one home the other way

parts.words: You must drive one home the other way
parts.note: a fastener with a reversed thread, turned anticlockwise to tighten it

explanation.surface: An instruction to take someone home by a different route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drive one home' suggests a car journey, but means turning a fastener in.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a fastener has a reverse thread, so it is tightened anticlockwise, opposite to normal.

clue.text: Fuss Hood had getting rid of churchman

indicators.note: getting rid of means the churchman's letters are removed from the words before

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a churchman's degree

explanation.surface: Robin Hood made a fuss when he got rid of a priest.
explanation.walkthrough: Both Ds are taken out of HOODHAD, one from each word.
explanation.definitionFit: A commotion or uproar is a fuss.

clue.text: See 22
Club a choirmaster formed with a famous composer

indicators.note: formed with means made from the very letters of the words, which here run across them

explanation.surface: A choirmaster founding a music society alongside a great composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' looks like a society, but its last letter begins the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Sebastian, the German Baroque master, is among the most famous composers.

clue.text: Skilful somersault over the top is involved

indicators.note: is involved means is contained within the words, running across them

explanation.surface: A clever gymnastic flip over the top of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over the top' reads as part of the somersault, but it is the definition, meaning excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive, effusive praise is called over the top.

clue.text: A king's rule, we're told, is put on trial

indicators.note: we're told signals that the phrase is replaced by one that is spoken alike

parts.note: a reign is a monarch's period of rule

explanation.surface: A monarch's rule, we hear, is in the dock.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge someone formally in court is to bring them to trial.

clue.text: A number of those undergoing 13 procedures

definitions.text: A number of those undergoing 13 procedures

parts.words: A number of those undergoing 13 procedures
parts.note: number read as numb-er, one who numbs patients during operations

explanation.surface: A count of patients having operations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' reads as a count, but it is 'numb-er', someone who numbs; 13 refers to the answer at 13-across.
explanation.definitionFit: The doctor who sends patients to sleep before surgery numbs them.
